_comment: The PC node's gate backend (#145, docs/LOCAL-RESOURCES.md "PC node (Strata)", docs/runbooks/PC-RTX3060-ENROLLMENT.md). Copy to ~/.config/cortados/local-backend.json ON THE PC (scripts/windows/install_pc_node.ps1 does it). Strata serves on 127.0.0.1:8080 only; the gate is the one door from the tailnet. The model is configuration (owner 2026-11-24: not final): another model is another strata.models entry, and strata.model names the one Strata serves. served_model_name must equal Strata's `aliases` entry for the model AND the id the provider's config gives it (tables/resources.example.json, the pc node).
_read_timeout_s: The gate's wait for each upstream read. A first turn after Strata's idle unload waits ~195 s for the load before the first byte; 600 s covers that and a long non-streamed answer at ~30 tok/s. Set the pc block's read_timeout_s on the provider host to the same.

strata._comment: max_inflight: Strata's --parallel is 1 on a 12 GB card, so the gate admits one turn at a time and answers a second with its retryable 529. context_tokens: the --max-context Strata was started with (Strata allocates the KV cache for it at load: the VRAM budget is spent there, so there is no per-request byte governor). upstream_ids: the names Strata's /v1/models may list for this model (default: served_model_name).

qwen36-35b-a3b-q4.name: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (UD-Q4_K_XL, RTX 3060)
qwen36-35b-a3b-q4._context_tokens: 48K: measured 2026-11-23/24 at 30.8 tok/s decode, 0.54 s TTFT, 11.6 of 12.0 GiB VRAM. 63,488 is the most that fits at Q4 on 12 GB and was not benchmarked; 128K does not fit.

node_policy._comment: Serve only while the owner is not using the PC (owner 2026-11-24). Each threshold's reason is in cortados_router/node_policy.py. activity_file: written every 5 s by the activity writer in the owner's session (task CortadOS-Activity); ~ is the account's profile.
node_policy._max_memory_load_pct: Off: with the model loaded Strata keeps ~19 GiB of experts in host RAM and free RAM measured 0.4 GiB (~99 % load), so any threshold would refuse all the time. Measure the PC's normal load first, then set one.
